listings.name: TWU Veteran Entrepreneur Grant
listings.organization: Texas Woman's University, Center for Women Entrepreneurs (Jane Nelson Institute)
listings.summary: Five $5,000 grants a year for veteran-owned small businesses in Texas to fund a growth project such as equipment, technology, inventory, property improvements or marketing. Winners complete a virtual small business training series, a business plan and three hours with a small business advisor.
listings.eligibility: A for-profit business (corporation, partnership, LLP, LLC or sole proprietorship) already formed, located and operating in Texas, at least 51% owned by one or more veterans who are U.S. citizens or permanent residents (honorable or general under honorable conditions discharge, transitioning active duty with a set discharge date, or Reserve or Guard). Nonprofits are not eligible. Owners must be current on taxes and licenses, have no pending litigation and no felony or dishonesty convictions. Prior CWE grant winners and anyone in a CWE program in the past year cannot apply. The pages conflict on women-only: the FAQ says any veteran-owned Texas business, but the guidelines ask for proof of 51% woman ownership and every published awardee has been a woman veteran. A 10% owner match is required.
listings.how_to_apply: Apply online through Submittable from the TWU Veteran Grant page during the application window. Submit formation documents, a Texas Veterans Commission document showing 51% or more ownership, a DD-214, and the CWE company background and project template with a budget showing exactly $5,000 in grant funds.
listings.deadline: The 2026 round ran January 27 to February 27, 2026, and is closed. 2027 dates are not announced.
listings.location: Online; Center for Women Entrepreneurs, Denton, Texas
listings.cost: Free to apply; a 10% owner match (cash or equipment, not borrowed) is required
listings.award: $5,000 per grant, five grants per round, paid in two installments
listings.unconfirmed: Whether men can apply. The FAQ says any veteran-owned Texas business, but the guidelines ask for proof of 51% woman ownership, and every published winner has been a woman veteran.
listings.source_title: Veteran Grant Guidelines | Texas Woman's University
listings.notes: Also read the Veteran Grant page, FAQ, 2026 Grant Dates page and the April 1, 2026 awardee announcement. Grant funds cannot pay wages, salaries, contract labor, monthly bills or sales tax. TWU issues a 1099 for grant funds. The guidelines do not mention equity or repayment; it is described as a grant. In 2023 the program awarded 22 grants of $5,000 to women veterans; in 2025 and 2026 it awarded five. The graphic's claims ($5,000, Texas veteran-owned, 10% owner match) match the official pages, but the women-ownership question should be confirmed with CWE before listing it as open to all veterans.
